item.title: Cliques, Quasi-Cliques, and Bicliques in Random Graphs: Sampling and Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2611.28307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the algorithmic problem of finding dense subgraphs - cliques, quasi-cliques, and bicliques - in Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs. While the extremal structure of cliques in $G(n,1/2)$ is well understood, efficiently locating large cliques remains a central algorithmic challenge. We introduce a new perspective on this problem: the classical Grimmett-McDiarmid greedy algorithm implicitly defines a near-uniform sampler over cliques of size $(1-o(1))\log n$. Building on this observation, we develop a sampling-based framework for finding larger cliques. In particular, for every $\eta>0$, we give an algorithm that finds a clique of size $(1+\eta)\log n$ in time $n^{(\eta^2/2+o(1))\log n}$ - the first smooth trade-off between clique size and running time in this regime, improving on the previously best-known running time of $n^{(1/2+o(1))\log n}$. We further show that improved sampling algorithms for cliques of size $(1+\eta)\log n$ translate into faster algorithms for finding a maximum clique. Beyond cliques, we give a deterministic algorithm that enumerates all maximum $\gamma$-quasi-cliques in $G(n,p)$ in time matching their count up to lower-order factors, and extend this to random bipartite graphs $G(n,n,p)$, establishing new concentration bounds for quasi-bicliques together with analogous enumeration algorithms. Finally, we study unbalanced bicliques in $G(n,n,p)$. For each $s \in [n]$, we obtain a concentration bound on the largest $t = t_{\max}(s)$ for which an $(s,t)$-biclique exists, and show that when $s = \omega(\log n)$, a simple greedy algorithm finds an $(s,(1-o(1))t_{\max}(s))$-biclique in linear time with high probability - demonstrating that greedy is near-optimal in this regime.
item.dc:creator: Thanh Le, A. Pavan, Xavier P\'erez-Gim\'enez, N. V. Vinodchandran

item.title: Tight Bounds for Rank Estimation in Turnstile Streams
item.description: arXiv:2611.28583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rank estimation in turnstile streams. A frequency vector $f$ over the universe $[U]$ receives insertions and deletions. Given a query $x\in[U]$, the goal is to estimate the rank $\sum_{u<x}f_u$ within additive error $\epsilon\|f\|_1$ with constant probability. The standard approach is Dyadic CountSketch by Luo, Wang, Yi and Cormode, using $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-1}\log^{3/2}U\log n)$ bits, where $n$ is the final $\ell_1$ norm of $f$. Bul\'anek, Kumar, Meka, Nelson, and Sarl\'os placed this approach in a matrix-factorization framework. They improved the space of Dyadic CountSketch to $O(\epsilon^{-1}\log^{3/2}U)$ words, and proved a lower bound of $\Omega(\epsilon^{-1}\log^2(\epsilon U))$ bits for all streaming algorithms when $U\le n\le U^{O(1)}$ and $\epsilon=U^{-1+\Omega(1)}$. This leaves a gap of $\sqrt{\log U}$. In this work, we fully determine the space cost of rank estimation up to an absolute constant. Our main result is a space lower bound for all streaming algorithms: for $0<\epsilon\le 1/8$ and $n\ge\log^2 U$, the space is at least $\Omega(\min\{\epsilon^{-1}L^{3/2}\log(2+n\epsilon/\sqrt{L}), \epsilon^{-2}\log U\log n, \log\binom{U+n}{n}\})$ bits, where $L=\log(2+U\epsilon)$. When $U\le n\le U^{O(1)}$ and $\epsilon=U^{-1+\Omega(1)}$, this simplifies to $\Omega(\min\{\epsilon^{-1}\log^{5/2}U, \epsilon^{-2}\log^2 U\})$ bits. Our proof uses a surprising hard distribution and novel information-theoretic techniques. The above bound matches Dyadic CountSketch when $n\ge U$ and $U^{-1+\Omega(1)}\le\epsilon\le O(1/\sqrt{\log U})$. The lower bound is also tight in the remaining regimes. For $\epsilon\ge(\log U)^{-1/2}$, there exists an algorithm that uses $O(\epsilon^{-2}\log U\log n)$ bits using $\ell_1$ samplers. For $\epsilon\le U^{-1+o(1)}$, we refine Dyadic CountSketch so that its space in bits matches the first term of the bound.
item.dc:creator: Yang S. Hu, Cheng Jiang, Yinchen Liu, Huacheng Yu

item.title: String Indexing for Maximal Gap-Bounded Occurrence Clusters
item.description: arXiv:2611.28734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeated occurrences of a pattern can form groups that reveal where repetition is concentrated in a text. We study how to find such groups efficiently when both the pattern $P$ and the distance threshold $G$ between occurrences are specified as query parameters. A maximal $G$-cluster of $P$ is a maximal block of at least two occurrences of $P$ whose consecutive starting positions differ by at most $G$. In this paper, we present indexes for reporting all cluster intervals and counting the clusters. For a text of length $n$ and a pattern of length $m$, we propose an $O(n\log n)$-space index that reports all maximal cluster intervals in $O(m+\log\log n+\mathit{output})$ time, where $\mathit{output}$ is the number of reported intervals, and that counts the clusters in $O(m+\log\log n)$ time. Restricting occurrences to those fully contained in a query substring preserves the reporting time using $O(n\log^2 n)$ space. Our indexes combine suffix-tree decompositions with geometric reporting queries on consecutive gaps.
item.dc:creator: Waseem Akram, Takuya Mieno

item.title: Towards a faster parameterized algorithm for Chordal Vertex Deletion
item.description: arXiv:2611.28948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The \textsc{Chordal Vertex Deletion} (\chvd{}) problem asks whether an input graph $G$ can be made chordal by removing at most $k$ vertices. When $k$ is taken as parameter, this problem is known to be fixed-parameter tractable \cite{M10,CM16}. However, it is still open whether \chvd{} admits a single-exponential FPT algorithm, i.e. an algorithm with running time $O(\alpha^k |V(G)|^c)$ for some constant $\alpha$ independent of $k$. Towards this goal, we describe an FPT algorithm for the compression version of \chvd{} with the following specification. Given an instance $I = (G,k,X)$ of the disjoint \chvd{} compression problem such that $|X| = k+1$, $G - X$ is chordal and its longest chordless path has length $L$, we solve $I$ in time $O((L+1)^{3k} k^2 |V(G)|^4)$.
item.dc:creator: Sylvain Guillemot

item.title: Exact edge cover by strict and non-strict temporal walks
item.description: arXiv:2611.28954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exact edge cover asks whether the edges of a temporal graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges can be partitioned into time-respecting walks with a prescribed number of walks starting at each vertex and, in the fixed-end variant, ending at each vertex. For non-strict walks, we prove that the problem is polynomially solvable by a new approach based on M-convexity, which also closes a gap in the proof sketch of an earlier static reduction. An orientation of the edges is realizable by walks exactly when walk counters stay non-negative and every snapshot component contains a walk, and only components with all degrees and counters even can violate the latter condition. Once a dead state is removed, the states of each such component form an M-convex set. This yields an augmenting path algorithm that returns walks or an infeasibility certificate, using at most $m/2$ augmentations and $O(n+nm^2)$ arithmetic operations with path-reversing re-orientation. The implementation was validated on small instances. For strict walks, we prove that the problem is NP-complete, already with six time labels for prescribed ends and two for free ends.
item.dc:creator: Duc Thien Quach, Manh Cuong Tran

item.title: A Simple Optimal Algorithm for Directed Multi-Failure Replacement Paths
item.description: arXiv:2611.29061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a graph $G = (V, E)$ and two vertices $s, t \in V$, the $f$-fault replacement paths ($f$-FRP) problem asks to compute, for every set $F$ of at most $f$ edges, the distance from $s$ to $t$ in $G \setminus F$. In this paper, we present a $3$-FRP algorithm in deterministic $O(n^3 \log n)$ time for directed weighted graphs. We also present a deterministic $O(n^4)$ time algorithm for $4$-FRP in directed weighted graphs, which implies a deterministic $O(n^f)$ time algorithm for $f$-FRP for every $f \ge 4$. Since the output size of $f$-FRP can be $\Theta(n^f)$, our algorithms are optimal for every $f \ge 4$ and nearly optimal for $f = 3$. Our algorithms also extend to the single-source and all-pairs settings with $f-1$ and $f-2$ failures, respectively, with the same time complexity as $f$-FRP. Moreover, our algorithms are remarkably simple.
item.dc:creator: Kaito Harada, Tatsuya Terao

item.title: Algorithms for Collaborative Truck-Multi-Drone Delivery in the En-Route Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.29102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study collaborative truck--multi-drone delivery in the en-route model, in which a truck moves continuously along a fixed straight-line path while drones serve $n$ off-route deliveries. For maximum coverage with $k$ drones, we prove that Sequential Greedy achieves an approximation guarantee of $1-(k/(k+1))^k$, which approaches $1-e^{-1}$. For $k=2$, our analysis is tight, with a matching $5/9$ instance. We refute the claimed exchange property for proper instances. For a new class of swap-monotone instances with distinct $x$-coordinates, we give an exact $O(n^2)$-time dynamic program for single-drone maximum coverage. For minimum fleet size, we prove NP-hardness and give an $O(1+\log(n/k^\ast))$-approximation using an integer residual bound, where $k^\ast$ is the optimum fleet size.
item.dc:creator: Jerry Mathew Oommen, Kelin Luo

item.title: On the Complexity of Orientable Domination
item.description: arXiv:2611.29202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The orientable domination number of an undirected graph $G$ is the maximum over all orientations $D$ of $G$ of the minimum size of a dominating set of $D$. In this paper, we look at the problem to decide if the orientable domination number of a given undirected graph $G$ is at least a given integer $\ell$. We show that this problem is complete for the class $\Sigma_2^P$, is fixed-parameter tractable by treewidth, and has a polynomial kernel parameterized by vertex cover number.
item.dc:creator: Hans L. Bodlaender, Tatsuya Gima, Yasuaki Kobayashi, Futaba Mizuno, Yuto Okada, Yota Otachi

item.title: A Local-to-Global Approximation Framework for Covering Disjointness-Compliable Set Families
item.description: arXiv:2611.29237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many network design problems can be formulated as covering a family of vertex sets by edges. We develop a local-to-global approximation framework for disjointness-compliable families with polynomial-time membership tests. A class of vertices is deficient if it belongs to the family and feasible otherwise. Our local problem seeks a minimum-cost tree that connects one deficient class to feasible classes so that their union is feasible. If this local problem admits a polynomial-time $\alpha$-approximation, then the covering problem admits a polynomial-time $(1+\varepsilon)(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{\alpha})^2$-approximation for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. Our algorithm first connects deficient vertices that are difficult to separate and then handles regions containing one deficient class at a time. To bound the total local cost, we compare the local trees with a feasible forest. We delete edges of this forest after using them in the bound, so each is counted at most once even when regions overlap. As applications, we obtain polynomial-time $(8+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithms for generalized point-to-point connection and multiroot quota tree, including multiroot $k$-minimum spanning tree. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first polynomial-time constant-factor approximations for both problems. We also obtain a randomized approximation for multiroot covering Steiner that has the same asymptotic ratio as the known approximation for its single-root version.
item.dc:creator: Jingyang Zhao, Mingyu Xiao

item.title: Exponential memory/query-complexity tradeoffs in high-accuracy feasibility problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.29320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove memory/query-complexity tradeoff lower bounds for the feasibility problem, where the goal is to find a point within an $\epsilon$-ball hidden in the unit $d$-dimensional ball, with access to a separation oracle. This problem admits three regimes: the low-accuracy regime $\epsilon\geq 1/\sqrt d$ where memory does not play a role, the medium-accuracy regime $1/\sqrt d\geq \epsilon\geq e^{-\Omega(d\ln d)}$ where prior works identified strong memory/query-complexity separations, and the high-accuracy regime $\epsilon\leq e^{-\Omega(d\ln d)}$ for which much less is known. In this regime, low-memory algorithms with significantly faster convergence rates than gradient descent have been developed in [BZJ24]: for accuracy $\epsilon$ and any $\delta\in[0,1]$, these require $d^{1+\delta}\ln \frac1\epsilon$ memory bits and use $\left(d\ln\frac1{\epsilon}\right)^{O(d^{1-\delta})}$ oracle queries. In comparison, gradient descent uses the same memory for $\delta=0$ but requires $1/\epsilon^2$ oracle queries. On the lower-bound side, no non-trivial memory/query-complexity tradeoff was known: the best lower bound remained the historical memory-independent bound $\Omega(d\ln \frac1\epsilon)$ from [NYD83]. We make progress towards characterizing the memory landscape in this high-accuracy regime by showing that for any $\delta\in[0,1]$, any algorithm with $d^{1+\delta}\ln\frac1{\epsilon}$ bits of memory uses at least $\left(d\ln\frac1{\epsilon}\right)^{\widetilde{\Omega}(d^{(1-\delta)/8})}$ oracle calls. This result justifies the seemingly peculiar exponential-in-$d$ dependence of oracle complexity for the aforementioned low-memory algorithms. In particular, our result shows that for high-accuracy feasibility problems, insufficient memory does result in an exponential price in the dimension for the query-complexity.
item.dc:creator: Jialin Yu, Mo\"ise Blanchard

item.title: Randomized MST Certification beyond Cacti
item.description: arXiv:2611.29623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study minimum spanning tree certification under explorable edge uncertainty. Edge weights lie in open intervals or singleton sets, and querying an edge reveals its weight at a known positive cost. On general graphs the best known randomized competitive ratio is $1+1/\sqrt2$, while the optimal ratio $3/2$ is known only for cacti. We go beyond cacti in two ways, with conditions that refer to the uncertain edges outside the upper-limit tree rather than to the graph alone. For unit query costs we give a $3/2$-competitive algorithm, which is best possible, whenever every block has at most two such edges; this includes all graphs whose blocks are cycles or theta graphs. The algorithm replaces the constant budget of the water-filling method by budgets chosen with lookahead to the next fundamental cycle. For arbitrary positive query costs and every fixed $k\ge1$, we obtain ratio $1+\sqrt{k/(2(k+1))}$ whenever every block has at most $k$ such edges, in particular when every block has cycle rank at most $k$. This is below $1+1/\sqrt2$ for every $k$, and we show that it is the best ratio attainable with a constant water-filling budget.
item.dc:creator: Sina Ghasemi Nezhad

item.title: Asymptotically Optimal Representation of Tree-Like Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.29624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how to represent a graph with $n$ nodes, $m=n+k=O(n)$ edges, and $h\le k$ nodes with more than one incoming edge in asymptotically optimal space, in a way that supports basic navigational operations quickly.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Fischer

item.title: Faster Directed SSSP on Digraphs with Random Sparse Supports or Few DFS Exceptions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study exact single-source shortest paths (SSSP) in directed graphs with $n$ vertices, $m$ arcs and nonnegative real weights, in the comparison-addition model. This paper continues our earlier work, which gave a deterministic algorithm that takes $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{1/4})$ time when $m=O(n)$ and $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{5/8})$ time when $m=\Theta(n\sqrt{\log\log n})$. Our two deterministic algorithms compute the distances on every input and take $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ time on two families of inputs, one per density. The support of an input is its underlying simple undirected graph. When $m=O(n)$, the first algorithm takes $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ time if no two simple cycles of the support with fewer than $P$ vertices share a vertex, where $P=\Theta(\sqrt{\log n})$ depends only on the support. For fixed $c>0$, a uniformly random graph with $n$ vertices and $\lfloor cn\rfloor$ edges has this property with probability at least $1-n^{-1+o(1)}$, and the bound then holds for every choice of one or both directions of each edge, all weights and every source. The second family is defined through the depth-first search tree of the support that starts at the source and visits neighbours in identifier order. For fixed $k\ge1$, call a set $Y$ of exceptional vertices $k$-feasible if, for each nonroot vertex, at most $k$ of its proper ancestors are joined to its subtree by arcs whose endpoints avoid $Y$ and whose underlying edges lie outside the DFS tree. Given $k$ but not such a set, the second algorithm takes, for every $k$-feasible set $Y$ of total out-degree $d^+(Y)$, time $O_k(n+m+(1+|Y|)\log n+\sqrt{(n+m)d^+(Y)\log n})$. When $m=\Theta(n\sqrt{\log\log n})$, this is $O_k(n\sqrt{\log n})$ if some $k$-feasible set has $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ vertices and total out-degree $O(n/\sqrt{\log\log n})$.
item.dc:creator: Valery (Binyamin), Grishin (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

item.title: An $n^{1/O(\log^* n)}$ Lower Bound for Online Coloring of $k$-Colorable Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.29672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In online coloring, the vertices of a graph arrive one at a time with their edges to earlier vertices, and each vertex must be colored irrevocably on arrival. For graphs promised to be $k$-colorable, with $k\ge 3$ fixed, the best deterministic algorithms use $n^{1-\Theta(1/k^2)}$ colors, while the best lower bound was Vishwanathan's $\Omega(\log^{k-1}n)$ from 1990 until Li recently proved $2^{\Omega((\log n)^{1/3}(\log\log n)^{2/3})}$. For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, we prove a lower bound of $n^{1/(\log^*n+3)}$ colors for deterministic online algorithms on $n$-vertex $k$-colorable graphs, and the same lower bound in expectation for randomized online algorithms. Both bounds hold on a single triangle-free $3$-colorable graph: even an algorithm that is shown this graph in advance, but is not told which of its vertices each arriving vertex is, can be forced to use this many colors by a suitable arrival order. The hard instances are iterated blow-ups of a clique, in which every vertex becomes a block of independent vertices and every edge a private server in the earlier block; each blow-up keeps the forced colors and replaces the chromatic number $\chi$ by about $\log\chi$, so about $\log^*n$ blow-ups bring it down to $k$. We also show that deterministic lower bounds for different values of $k\ge 3$ are polynomially equivalent, and that no adversary presenting such iterated blow-ups can force more than $n^{1/(\log^*n-O(1))}$ colors. All numbered results are formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Sajad Faghfoor Maghrebi

item.title: Improved Approximation Algorithms for Multi-Path TSP and Ordered TSP
item.description: arXiv:2611.29809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Multi-Path TSP, given a metric and $k$ pairs of vertices $(s_i,t_i)$, where $k$ is part of the input, we seek $s_i$--$t_i$ paths of minimum total length that together visit all vertices. Ratios below $2$ were known only for graphic metrics and special cases such as multiple depots ($s_i=t_i$); in general metrics, the best ratio was $1+2e^{-1/2}\approx2.213$, by a randomized algorithm of B\"ohm, Friggstad, M\"omke and Spoerhase [SODA 2025]. We give a deterministic algorithm with ratio $\frac{5e-2}{3e-2}<1.8833$ relative to a restriction of their LP relaxation, bounding its integrality gap by the same constant. For Ordered TSP, where a tour must visit $k$ given vertices in a prescribed cyclic order, we compute tours within $1+\frac{e}{2(e-1)}<1.7910$ times the value of the LP relaxation of Armbruster, Mnich and N\"agele [APPROX 2024], improving $\frac32+\frac1e\approx1.868$ on both the ratio and the integrality gap. Our algorithms sample a tree for every pair (for Ordered TSP, every two consecutive given vertices) from an LP solution, but keep only the path between the two endpoints. Our main lemma shows that, for arbitrary nonnegative edge weights, a cheapest forest connecting all vertices to these paths has expected weight at most $1/e$ times that of a cheapest forest rooted at the endpoints plus $(1-1/e)$ times the expected weight of the discarded branches. For Multi-Path TSP, we use the weights of a primal--dual growth process that Zhao, Liu and Xiao [arXiv 2026] designed for multiple depots; in these weights, the connecting forest also pays for part of correcting its degree parities.
item.dc:creator: Morteza Alimi, Michael Ruderer

item.title: Tight Query Depth of Recursive Randomized Greedy MIS
item.description: arXiv:2611.29854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The randomized greedy maximal independent set (RGMIS) algorithm processes vertices in a uniformly random order and greedily constructs an MIS. Its recursive formulation decides whether a vertex belongs to this MIS by querying lower-ranked neighbors in increasing rank order, stopping when a neighbor in the MIS is found. We prove that, on every $n$-vertex graph, this recursive algorithm has $O(\log n)$ query depth with high probability, even without memoization. The bound holds simultaneously for all starting vertices and is asymptotically tight even on bipartite graphs. The proof combines a bound on the total expected number of query paths with an exposure argument: paths with many two-edge shortcuts are unlikely, while the remaining paths admit sufficiently many applications of a two-hop probability bound.
item.dc:creator: Slobodan Mitrovi\'c, Wen-Horng Sheu

item.title: Trusted Advice for Scheduling on Unrelated Machines
item.description: arXiv:2611.29883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scheduling on unrelated parallel machines under standard objectives, such as makespan minimization or max-min fairness, has posed fundamental theoretical challenges for decades. A prominent example is the longstanding factor 2 approximation barrier for the Min Makespan problem established by Lenstra, Shmoys, and Tardos (1990). We investigate these fundamental challenges within the framework of algorithms with trusted advice. We consider a setting in which a trusted oracle is accessed once and reveals partial but entirely accurate structural information about an optimal solution. This framework allows us to quantify the improvements in approximation guarantees enabled by various trusted advice. We formalize a hierarchy of trusted advice oracles, ranging from a strong oracle that reveals the exact assignments of long jobs to a weaker oracle that indicates only which machines process such jobs. By exploiting this information, we obtain approximation guarantees beyond the classical worst-case barriers. In particular, we show that even the weakest oracle improves the approximation ratio for Min Makespan to $\sqrt{3}\approx 1.732$. We also obtain improved ratios of $(\sqrt{33}+1)/4\approx 1.686$ and $(5\sqrt{7})/8 \approx 1.654$ for Restricted Assignment and Graph Balancing, respectively. For the max-min fairness objective, known as the Santa Claus problem, we obtain a 2-approximation using our weak oracle. Finally, we show that these problems remain NP-hard to approximate within certain constant factors even with the trusted advice oracles considered. Interestingly, for the Santa Claus problem, we show a lower bound of 2 which is tight and matches the classical oracle-free bound.
item.dc:creator: Baruch Schieber, Hadas Shachnai, Tami Tamir

item.title: Constrained Online Selection with Predictions: Matroid Secretary, Knapsack, and Matching
item.description: arXiv:2611.29952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study learning-augmented algorithms for constrained online selection problems, including the secretary problem under matroid and knapsack constraints, and the edge-weighted online bipartite matching problem with random vertex arrivals. In each, items arrive in a uniformly random order, and their values are revealed only on arrival. The goal is to select a set of items with nearly maximum total value, subject to the constraints (matroid, knapsack, or matching). In the learning-augmented setting, item value predictions are given in advance. We seek algorithms that are both consistent, in that accurate predictions lead to near-optimal selection, and robust, in that they obtain strong worst-case bounds even when predictions are inaccurate. Building on work of Fujii and Yoshida (2024) on the learning-augmented secretary problem, we study a method that follows the predicted optimum until an item with a large enough prediction error is observed. At that point, it reverts to running a worst-case competitive algorithm. We make a simple but critical modification: the first item with a large prediction error is selected with a carefully chosen probability. With this modification, we prove a general result, showing that if the underlying worst-case algorithm is $\alpha$-competitive for $\alpha\in(0,1]$, this approach achieves competitive ratio $\max\{\frac{\alpha}{2(1+\alpha)},\frac{1-\epsilon}{1+\epsilon}\}$, where $\epsilon$ is the maximum relative error of any prediction. That is, the algorithm is perfectly consistent, achieving competitive ratio $1$ as $\epsilon \to 0$, and robust up to a constant factor relative to the worst-case baseline. For all three problems we study, $\alpha = 1/e$, and our result is the first to achieve consistency and constant-factor robustness. We hope that our general analysis framework can be applied to other learning-augmented online decision-making problems.
item.dc:creator: Hedyeh Beyhaghi, Tao Zixu He, Cameron Musco

item.title: Optimal Private Gaussian Multi-sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.30146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give polynomial-time algorithms for Gaussian multi-sampling under approximate $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy, with optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors. Our main construction uses $\widetilde{O}(m+d\sqrt{m}/\varepsilon)$ independent input samples from a $d$-dimensional Gaussian $P$ with unknown mean and covariance to generate $m$ exactly independent outputs. Their joint distribution is $\alpha$-close in total variation to $P^{\otimes m}$. Our lower bounds hold even for dependent outputs under the same joint accuracy guarantee, showing that exact independence incurs no additional sample cost beyond logarithmic factors. The single-sampler of Iverson, Kamath, and Mouzakis [COLT 2025] uses $\widetilde{O}(d/\varepsilon)$ input samples. Running it on a separate input dataset for each of $m$ outputs therefore costs $\widetilde{O}(md/\varepsilon)$ in total. Our construction reduces this dimension-dependent sample cost from linear to square-root dependence on the number of outputs. Our approach builds on the stable weighted statistics of Brown, Hopkins, and Smith [COLT 2023], also used for Gaussian single-sampling by Iverson, Kamath, and Mouzakis. To control privacy loss when the entire batch shares these statistics, we compare the joint output densities and obtain a privacy bound that scales with the square root of the batch size. The stability step downweights influential records and can reject the entire batch. Both actions can make the outputs dependent. Our correction restores exact independence while preserving differential privacy and joint accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Raoof Zare Moayedi, Mohammad Hossein Yassaee, Javad B. Ebrahimi

item.title: Location-Aware Matching Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.30206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Edit distance is the standard measure of string similarity, but its quadratic-time complexity is prohibitive for long strings. Popular linear-time alternatives, such as the $q$-gram distance, or the average common substring measure (ACS) that is based on matching statistics (MS), consider the substrings shared by the two input strings but not where they occur in each string. Yet in many real-world applications, e.g., when comparing document versions or co-recorded time series, a shared substring is really relevant only if its occurrences are close in position. We introduce Location-Aware Matching Statistics (LAMAS). Given strings $X$ and $Y$ and a displacement tolerance $d$, LAMAS reports, for every position $i$ of $Y$, the longest substring starting at $i$ that occurs in $X$ at a position $j$ with $|j-i|\le d$, together with the displacement $(j-i)$. MS is the special case of LAMAS with unbounded $d$. Our main result is an algorithm that solves LAMAS in $\mathcal{O}(n)$ time and space for strings of length at most $n$ and any $d$; this is optimal and matches the complexity of MS. The algorithm reduces LAMAS to predecessor and successor queries over a sliding window of suffix ranks and answers them in linear total time via a window decomposition and interval union-find. Experiments on 20 real datasets and synthetic data show that LAMAS substantially improves over MS and $q$-gram distance in similarity-based classification, top-$K$ retrieval, and clustering. It is competitive with edit distance and a constrained dynamic time warping variant in classification and generally outperforms a state-of-the-art method for top-$K$ retrieval under edit distance. Finally, our implementation of the main algorithm for LAMAS scales linearly in $n$ and does not slow down as $d$ grows.
item.dc:creator: Lorraine A. K. Ayad, Grigorios Loukides, Solon P. Pissis

item.title: Weighted Flow Time Does Not Admit Constant-Competitive Randomized Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2611.30319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study online preemptive scheduling on a single machine with the objective of minimizing the total weighted flow time. Bansal and Chan (SODA 2009) showed that no deterministic online algorithm is $O(1)$-competitive for this problem. We show that no randomized online algorithm is $O(1)$-competitive against an oblivious adversary either. This settles the remaining case of the long-standing question whether the problem admits an $O(1)$-competitive online algorithm. Quantitatively, every randomized online algorithm has a competitive ratio in $\Omega(\min\{\log\log W,\log\log\log\min\{P,D,n\}\})$, where $n$ is the number of jobs and $W$, $P$, and $D$ are the ratios of the largest to the smallest job weight, size, and density (weight divided by size), respectively. The lower bound also holds with high probability, with the same asymptotic dependence on the instance parameters. For every $\rho\ge1$ and every randomized online algorithm, there is an instance on which the cost of the algorithm is at least $\rho$ times the optimal cost with probability at least $1-2^{-2^\rho}$. Both lower bounds hold even if the algorithm knows in advance the size and weight of every job in release order and, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, every interarrival time up to a factor of $1+\varepsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Lindermayr

item.title: First-Order Entropic Sampling of Words with Prescribed Letter Counts in Linear Time
item.description: arXiv:2611.30332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We sample, exactly and uniformly, a word of length n over the alphabet {0, . . . , r} in which the letter j occurs a prescribed positive number k j of times, from a source of fair random bits. Every exact sampler reads on average at least H = log 2 (___ n k0,...,kr )___ bits. We give a sampler that reads on average at most H fresh bits, whatever r and the counts, and that performs O(n) bit operations on average over every fixed alphabet, in a bit-RAM in which a memory access costs O(1) while arithmetic is charged bit by bit. Both bounds are optimal: the first one to first order, the second one up to a constant factor, since writing the output already costs $\Theta$(n). The sampler writes the word as a Huffman tree of independent binary words, and samples each of them in one of two ways. Binary words with few ones are generated by random insertions; the rank of each inserted letter among its copies, which the Fisher-Yates shuffle generates for nothing, is uniform and independent of the word, and is given back to a recycling source of uniform integers, where it pays for the next insertions. Binary words with many ones are generated by MergeShuffle driven by blocks of $\Theta$(log n) bits of entropy; a block is decoded by locating only its ones when the minority letter is rare, and otherwise, its number of ones being concentrated, by a precomputed table of the blocks of typical type, of size O( $\sqrt$ n log 4 n), the rare atypical blocks being decoded slowly.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Bodini (LAGA), Francis Durand (LAGA)

item.title: Optimizing Diameter of r-Gather under Connectivity Constraints from Convex to Connected
item.description: arXiv:2611.30875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $r$-gather problem partitions the nodes of an edge-weighted graph into clusters of at least $r$ nodes each. The problem is NP-hard, and known approximation algorithms may return clusters whose induced subgraphs are disconnected. We therefore require each cluster to be connected, or even convex in the existential sense that some shortest path between any two of its members stays inside the cluster. We add a parameterized $\alpha$-ratio-convex variant that interpolates between the two by bounding the induced stretch by a factor $\alpha$. We measure the cost of a clustering by its diameter, the largest pairwise distance within a cluster, rather than by the radius as in the classical formulation. We show that the variants form a hierarchy, that they remain NP-hard in general, and that none of them admits a polynomial-time $(2-\varepsilon)$-approximation unless P=NP. Our main algorithmic result is a polynomial-time algorithm for convex $r$-gather on trees. This contrasts with connected $k$-diameter, which remains hard even on star-like connectivity graphs. On general weighted graphs, we give a $4$-approximation for connected $r$-gather. Extending the tree algorithm to tree decompositions, we obtain an exact algorithm for connected $r$-gather that is fixed-parameter tractable in the treewidth together with $d$ and $r$. Finally, we relate the $\alpha$-ratio-convex variant to $t$-spanners, which yields further approximation guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Thomas C. van Dijk, Wolf Ki{\ss}ler, Lukas Pl\"atz, Marena Richter, Jonathan Rollin

item.title: Tight Analysis for Online Generalized Network Design with Power Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the online generalized network design problem with heterogeneous power costs. Here, a sequence of $N$ requests arrive online, each of which needs to be assigned to some subset of available resources $E$. Each resource $e\in E$ has its own coefficient $\xi_e>0$ and exponent $p_e\ge 1$, where the cost of a load vector $L\in \mathbb{R}^E_+$ is $\Phi(L)=\sum_{e\in E}\xi_e L_e^{p_e}$. We provide a simple analysis for the natural greedy algorithm that $\tau$-approximately minimizes the increase in $\Phi$ for each online request. Our competitive ratio is at most $(\frac{p}{\ln 2})^p$ when $\tau=1$ and is roughly $(\tau p)^p$ as $\tau$ grows large; here $p=\max_{e\in E} p_e$. This improves over a prior competitive ratio of $2(e\tau p)^p$ that relied on a modified greedy algorithm and a more complex analysis. Moreover, our bound (with $\tau=1$) is asymptotically optimal: it matches the $(1.443p)^p$ lower bound for deterministic online algorithms. We also provide a nuanced exponent-dependent bound that, combined with prior results, provides an improved competitive ratio for (dis)economies of scale cost functions; here, the cost of resource $e$ has the form $\sigma_e + \xi_e\cdot x^{p_e}$ if $x>0$ (and zero if $x=0$). These results apply to several fundamental network problems such as multicommodity routing (where $\tau=1$), Steiner tree connectivity (where $\tau=1.39$) and directed Steiner connectivity (where $\tau$ is poly-logarithmic).
item.dc:creator: Karl Li, Yanzhi Li, Viswanath Nagarajan

item.title: Optimal Matroid Prophets against Almighty Adversaries and Delegation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an optimal one-half matroid prophet inequality against an almighty ordering adversary: the adversary observes every realized value before choosing the arrival order, whereas the algorithm sees values only as they arrive and must accept irrevocably. The algorithm is deterministic, and its guarantee holds against the stronger ex-ante relaxation. Before any values are revealed, it partitions the ground set, replaces the matroid by a stricter direct sum of minors, and fixes one threshold for each part. It then accepts greedily subject to these fixed tests. The main lemma bounds the expected value of the least valuable basis of the eligible elements. An element contributes either through the rank spanned by eligible elements or through excess value that every eligible basis must retain. This bound holds simultaneously for all bases and therefore permits the arrival order to depend on the entire realization. The same construction gives a deterministic, agent-oblivious mechanism for (possibly correlated) matroid delegation, improving the $1/4$ guarantee to the optimal $1/2$ factor. The principal values are independent, while the strictly positive agent utilities may have arbitrary dependence on the principal values and on one another. The guarantee holds for every best response, including ties resolved against the principal. Both factors are tight already in rank one. For rational finite-support distributions, preprocessing takes polynomial time; each eligible online arrival requires at most one query to the original matroid's independence oracle.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Abdi, Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Danny Mittal

item.title: Planar Graphs Embed into Graphs with Treewidth $O(\log n /\epsilon)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a stochastic embedding of $n$-vertex planar graphs into graphs of treewidth $O(\log n/\epsilon)$ and expected distortion $1+\epsilon$ for any parameter $\epsilon \in (0,1)$. This result yields randomized polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTASes) for a broad class of connectivity problems on planar graphs, including the $k$-MST problem. The treewidth bound is asymptotically optimal and settles a conjecture of Chang, Cohen-Addad, Conroy, Le, Ma. Pilipczuk, and Mi. Pilipczuk (2025). The key idea is a new construction of a stochastic balanced cut of size $O(\log n/\epsilon)$ and expected distortion $1+\epsilon/\log n$ for every edge. We construct these cuts using the minimax principle, an approach that differs significantly from existing cut constructions based on a random clustering hierarchy. Our embedding extends to minor-free graphs using the Robertson-Seymour decomposition, giving the same treewidth bound. Using this decomposition, we obtain the first randomized PTASes for many connectivity problems in minor-free graphs, including the Steiner tree problem and its prize-collecting variant.
item.dc:creator: Hung Le

item.title: A Deterministic Linear Time Algorithm for Minimum Spanning Tree
item.description: arXiv:2611.31187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there is a deterministic linear time algorithm for the minimum spanning tree problem, thereby settling this problem, and providing the first improvement since the work of Chazelle (JACM 2000). Our work proceeds by showing that the deterministic comparison complexity of the minimum spanning tree problem is linear, whereby a known reduction of Pettie and Ramachandran (JACM 2002) immediately implies a linear time algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Sanjeev Khanna, Aaron Putterman, Junkai Song

item.title: Cop-Win Edge Completion: Hardness, Structure, and Parameterized Algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2611.31191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Cop-Win Edge Completion: given a graph $G$, find the minimum number $\copfill(G)$ of edges whose addition lets one cop capture a visible robber. We first give an exact reduction from Dominating Set, constructing for every nonempty graph $H$ a graph $G_H$ on $2|V(H)|+2$ vertices with $\copfill(G_H)=\gamma(H)$. This resolves a complexity question of Mertzios et al. and implies NP-completeness even for connected graphs of diameter two with a dominating edge and domination number two. Interestingly, while Minimum Fill-in is fixed-parameter tractable in the number $k$ of added edges, Cop-Win Edge Completion, whose target class strictly contains the connected chordal graphs, is W[2]-hard parameterized by $k$, even by $k+\gamma(G)$. We then give two lower bounds. The first, $\copfill(G)\ge 2n-m-b-c-1$, where $n,m,b,c$ count vertices, edges, nontrivial blocks, and components, is tight for partial 2-trees, giving a linear-time algorithm for the optimum value and a quadratic-time construction; for outerplanar graphs, an optimum completion preserving outerplanarity is found in linear time. The second, based on the cycle space modulo the subspace generated by triangles, gives $\copfill(G)=c-1+\sum_{i=1}^r(\ell_i-3)$ for block-cactus graphs with long cycle blocks of lengths $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$. We also show how the optimum behaves under disjoint unions and joins, yielding a polynomial-time algorithm for $P_4$-sparse graphs, including cographs, and exact formulas for complete multipartite graphs. In contrast to partial 2-trees and block-cactus graphs, an optimum cop-win completion can be much smaller than a minimum chordal one, already on complete bipartite graphs. Finally, we give FPT algorithms for $k+\mathrm{nd}(G)$, for the twin-cover number $t$ alone in time $2^{O(t^3)}n^{O(1)}$, and for $k+\mathrm{tw}(G)$.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Adak

item.title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification
item.description: arXiv:2611.28399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can we estimate the probability of an event chosen after seeing the data, without using any fresh samples? Its empirical probability can be arbitrarily misleading, while learning the entire distribution to constant accuracy requires $\Theta(d)$ samples on a domain of size $d$. We show that $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d})$ samples suffice for constant mean squared error, provided the rule choosing the event is known. More generally, our estimator handles arbitrary $[0,1]$-valued queries and runs in polynomial time given evaluation access to the rule. This sample complexity matches the known lower bound up to logarithmic factors and resolves the open question posed by Feldman, Kale, Raman, Talwar, and Tewari (arXiv:2610.41244). Our estimation framework relies on a new combination of sample amplification (arXiv:1904.12053 and arXiv:2201.04315) with distribution learning via online optimization. Our estimator achieves mean squared error $O(d^{3/4}/n)$ when $d\leq n$ and $\widetilde{O}(d^{1/4}/\sqrt{n})$ when $d>n$. We complement this with a lower bound of $\Omega(\min\{1,\sqrt{d}/n\})$ on the mean squared error. Using our framework, we also design an efficient estimator for data-dependent queries on Gaussian distributions with unknown mean and identity covariance. Finally, we show that a smoothed variant of the problem is much (exponentially) easier. For discrete distributions, if the sample size is chosen uniformly from $\{n,\ldots,2n-1\}$, then $n=O(\log d)$ suffices for constant mean squared error.
item.dc:creator: Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Mahbod Majid, Kunal Talwar

item.title: A $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-Approximation for Weighted 3-Set Packing
item.description: arXiv:2611.28541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a deterministic $(3/2+\varepsilon)$-approximation for weighted $3$-set packing, for every fixed rational $\varepsilon>0$, improving on the 1.6908-approximation reported by Tong and Xu (2026). The algorithm has two phases. It first performs bounded local search using a rounded $12/7$-power potential. It then combines compatible exchanges that insert at most three sets and increase the original weight. The analysis relates the gap left by the first phase to the gain available to the second phase. We prove a structural inequality that bounds the weight of a comparison packing by $3/2$ times the current weight plus one sixth of a sum of small-exchange gains. Each gain accounts for all sets that the exchange must delete. A greedy rule recovers enough of these gains to obtain the approximation guarantee. We derive the structural bound from local optimality by analyzing finite computation trees and averaging the error caused by their limited depth. The running time is $n^{4^{O(1/\varepsilon)}}\operatorname{poly}(L)$, where $n$ is the number of input sets and $L$ is the input encoding length. The same guarantee holds for maximum-weight independent set in induced $K_{1,4}$-free graphs.
item.dc:creator: Changjun Wang, Daorong Yu, Wei Yu

item.title: Tight Mistake-Abstention Tradeoffs for Sequential Prediction under Adversarial Injections
item.description: arXiv:2611.28579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the sequential prediction problem introduced by Goel et al. (2023), where an adversary can inject arbitrarily many corrupted instances in an i.i.d. stream from a clean distribution $\mu$, while the learner is allowed to abstain from making a prediction at no cost if the current instance was indeed injected. When $\mu$ is unknown, Yu and Blanchard (2026) show a polynomial tradeoff between mistakes and false abstentions for classes with finite VC dimension and oblivious adversaries, but still leave open a significant gap between upper and lower bounds in their tradeoff landscape. In this paper, we propose the weighted shattering potential, and based on variants of this potential, provide gap-closing algorithms that essentially characterize the tradeoffs under various settings of interest: When $\mu$ is known, our algorithm improves over Goel et al. (2023) and achieves their conjectured $O(d\log T)$ mistake bound; When $\mu$ is unknown, for oblivious adversary, our guarantees are tight both in $T$ and in terms of the VC dimension $d$, which completely characterizes the abstention-mistake tradeoff in this setting and gives an $O(\sqrt{dT})$ balanced rate. For adaptive adversary, our results are tight up to $\operatorname{poly}(dD\log T)$ factors for structured classes with finite so-called reduction dimension $D$. Our guarantees also extend to censored feedback, where the label is hidden after an abstention.
item.dc:creator: Mo\"ise Blanchard, Ezra Edelman, Surbhi Goel, Shyam Narayanan, Jialin Yu

item.title: Two Rounds Are Already Hard for Loop-Free Updates of Routing Trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.29695v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Updating a routing tree can create loops even when the old and new trees lead to the same destination. A controller chooses which routers update in each round, but their updates may finish in any order. Strong loop freedom therefore requires every partial completion to be acyclic. We show that deciding whether two rounds suffice is NP-complete, even when a safe three-round schedule is supplied. The proof is a linear-size reduction from 3-SAT with one old clause spine and four routers per variable. Three types of mixed cycles enforce consistent literal choices and clause satisfaction. For every nonempty input formula, the constructed instance needs exactly two rounds if the formula is satisfiable and exactly three otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Klaus-Tycho Foerster

item.title: A Deterministic Polynomial-Query Protocol for Envy-Free Cake Cutting
item.description: arXiv:2611.30002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a deterministic protocol that divides a heterogeneous cake completely and without envy among $n$ agents using $O(n^6\log n)$ Robertson--Webb queries in the worst case. Valuations may be arbitrary nonnegative, nonatomic measures, and bundles may be disconnected. The protocol makes $O(n)$ calls to certified trimming, which uses $O(n^5\log n)$ queries on $n$ pieces. In a certified trim, each agent receives the end part, or suffix, of a different piece without envy, and every shortened piece has a witness tie leading back to a whole piece. At each step, the witness values the shortened suffix exactly as much as her own. For pieces of positive interval length with strictly increasing suffix values, the retained suffix lengths are unique, although their holders may differ. Candidate assignments share a table of value and cut queries. If the coordinatewise median of their value estimates fails a matching test, the test identifies an agent whose value is underestimated, ruling out at least half the remaining assignments. A weighted median of cut marks lets one repair step remove a small envy while allocating almost all of the residue. For complete envy-free chore allocation, the query bound is $O(n^7\log n)$.
item.dc:creator: Haris Aziz

item.title: Quantum simulation of low-temperature impurity models
item.description: arXiv:2611.30187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum impurity models, which describe a small but strongly-interacting subsystem coupled to a large noninteracting bath, are the computational core of dynamical mean field theory and play an important role in simulating strongly correlated materials. We develop quantum algorithms for efficiently simulating these models at low temperatures and with high precision. For any impurity model on $n$ fermionic modes with fixed impurity size: (1) We give a quantum algorithm that prepares the thermal state at inverse temperature $\beta$ to precision $\delta$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\beta,\log(1/\delta))$. This algorithm is the first to achieve both polynomial scaling in the inverse temperature and polylogarithmic scaling in the precision. When the Hamiltonian has an inverse-polynomial spectral gap, our quantum algorithm prepares its ground state to precision $\delta$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log(1/\delta))$. (2) We further give a quantum algorithm that prepares a purification of the thermal state in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\beta,\log(1/\delta))$. Using this purification, we estimate static and dynamical properties with error $\delta$ in time polynomial in $n$ and $\beta$ and linear in $1/\delta$ up to polylogarithmic factors, achieving the Heisenberg scaling. Our algorithms build on quantum Gibbs samplers, which are quantum analogues of Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. By using global jump operators instead of local ones, we avoid the $\exp(\beta)$ overhead commonly associated with quantum Gibbs samplers, making them efficient for impurity models even at low temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqing Jiang, Nathan Ju

item.title: Quantitative Convergence of Hit-and-Run Beyond Log-Concavity via Variational Hypocoercivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.30691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the convergence to equilibrium of Hit-and-Run, a popular generalisation of the Gibbs sampler. To this end, we establish a novel connection between Hit-and-Run and the theory of variational hypocoercivity, an approach to establish convergence of continuous-time Markov processes. To bridge the gap between the discrete-time Hit-and-Run chain and hypocoercivity, we introduce Hit-and-Langevin, a continuous-time Markov process that approximates Hit-and-Run in an appropriate sense. Using the second-order lift and flow Poincar\'e inequality formulation of variational hypocoercivity, we show convergence of Hit-and-Langevin and deduce a lower bound on the spectral gap of Hit-and-Run. Notably, our analysis seamlessly extends beyond the extensively studied setting of log-concave target distributions, marking the first substantial departure from this setting beyond quasi-log-concave and uniform distributions. More broadly, this work demonstrates that discrete, non-local dynamics, such as Hit-and-Run, can be made amenable to powerful analytical methods, such as variational hypocoercivity.
item.dc:creator: Francis L\"orler, Stefan Oberd\"orster

item.title: Via a New LP Relaxation: Stronger Performance Guarantees for WSEPT, and an LP-Based Proof of Kawaguchi & Kyan
item.description: arXiv:2611.30731v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a new linear programming relaxation for minimizing the total weighted completion time on identical parallel machines. Its right-hand side is supermodular, so the relaxation can be solved by a greedy algorithm. We show that the WSPT rule is within a factor $\frac{1}{2}(1 + \sqrt{2})$ of the optimal LP value. This bounds the integrality gap of the relaxation and gives a short, LP-based proof of the tight bound of Kawaguchi and Kyan on the performance of WSPT. We then turn to the stochastic version of the problem, in which processing times are independent random variables whose squared coefficients of variation are at most~$\Delta$. A variance-corrected version of the new LP relaxation is valid for all non-anticipatory policies, and we show that WSEPT is within a factor $1 + (1 + \Delta)/(3 + \sqrt{7 + 2 \Delta})$ of it for $\Delta \ge 1$, for any number of machines. This is $O(\sqrt\Delta)$, whereas all previous guarantees for this problem grow linearly in $\Delta$. Up to a constant factor, our bound matches the known $\Omega(\sqrt\Delta)$ lower bound for WSEPT. For $\Delta \le 1$, we recover the best known bounds.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian von Aspern, Andreas S. Schulz, Eugenio Vairo

item.title: A Matrix Lee-Sidford Barrier and Faster Semidefinite Programming
item.description: arXiv:2611.30757v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a matrix analog of the Lee-Sidford barrier for semidefinite programming (SDP) with $m$ equality constraints and $n$-by-$n$ matrices. The barrier has self-concordance parameter $\widetilde{O}(m)$, so short-step interior-point methods require only $\widetilde O(\sqrt m)$ iterations. We also show that our matrix Lee-Sidford barrier can be implemented efficiently by developing a randomized algorithm that solves SDPs with $m\leq n$ to accuracy $\epsilon$ in $(n^{\omega+o(1)}+n^2m^{3/2+o(1)})\operatorname{polylog}(1/\epsilon)$ time, where $\omega\leq 9/4$ is the matrix multiplication exponent, achieving the fastest known running time in this regime.
item.dc:creator: Zhao Song, Ruizhe Zhang

item.title: Nearly-Tight Oracle Complexity of Packing and Covering Linear Programs
item.description: arXiv:2611.30805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We settle the deterministic oracle complexity of packing and covering linear programs, as measured by the number of oracle queries to the constraint matrix modeled by left and right matrix-vector products, up to a logarithmic factor. We do so by providing nearly-matching upper and lower bounds. Our algorithm breaks the $1/\epsilon^2$ barrier of width-independent, $(1+\epsilon)$-multiplicative error parallel solvers from prior work, improving the scaling with the error $\epsilon >0$ to $1/\epsilon,$ with total number of arithmetic operations scaling near-linearly with $1/\epsilon$ and the number of nonzero entries of the constraint matrix.
item.dc:creator: Jelena Diakonikolas, Guy Kornowski

item.title: Closed Repeats
item.description: arXiv:2410.00209v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Much research in stringology focuses on structures that can, in a way, ``grasp'' repeats (substrings that occur multiple times) as, for example, the so-called runs, a.k.a. maximal repetitions, compactly describe all tandem repeats. In this paper we introduce closed repeats: given a string $s$, its non-empty substring $s[i\,..\,j]$ is a right (left) closed repeat if its closest occurrence $s[i'\,..\,j']$ with $i' > i$ cannot be ``extended'' to the right (respectively, left) matching $s[j{+}1] = s[j'{+}1]$ (respectively, $s[i{-}1] = s[i'{-}1]$); the repeat is closed if it is both left and right closed. We note that the closed repeats correspond to the maximal closed substrings recently proposed by Badkobeh, De Luca, Fici, and Puglisi and they include all runs as a special case. We prove that the number of right/left closed repeats is $O(n \log n)$, where $n$ is the length of $s$, and we show that this bound is tight. The (right/left) closed repeats can be computed in the optimal time $O(n\log n)$; as we prove, the time cannot be lower than $\Omega(n\log\sigma)$ over a general size-$\sigma$ alphabet even if there are only $O(n)$ closed repeats. As an application, we describe data structures using the closed repeats for substring queries: finding the period of the substring provided it is ``periodic'', finding the longest repeat in the substring, computing the rightmost LZ77 parsing of the substring.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Kosolobov

item.title: LLM Query Scheduling with Prefix Reuse and Latency Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2502.04677v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) in online settings requires optimizing inference performance under stringent latency constraints, particularly the time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT). This paper focuses on the query scheduling problem for LLM inference with prefix reuse, a technique that leverages shared prefixes across queries to reduce computational overhead. Our work reveals previously unknown limitations of the existing first-come-first-serve (FCFS) and longest-prefix-match (LPM) scheduling strategies with respect to satisfying latency constraints. We present a formal theoretical framework for LLM query scheduling under RadixAttention, a prefix reuse mechanism that stores and reuses intermediate representations in a radix tree structure. Our analysis establishes the NP-hardness of the scheduling problem with prefix reuse under TTFT constraints and proposes a novel scheduling algorithm, $k$-LPM, which generalizes existing methods by balancing prefix reuse and fairness in query processing. Theoretical guarantees demonstrate that $k$-LPM achieves improved TTFT performance under realistic traffic patterns captured by a data generative model. Empirical evaluations in a realistic serving setting validates our findings, showing significant reductions in P99 TTFT compared to baseline methods.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025)
item.dc:creator: Gregory Dexter, Shao Tang, Ata Fatahi Baarzi, Qingquan Song, Tejas Dharamsi, Aman Gupta

item.title: Scheduling in Queueing Systems with Uncertain and Evolving Holding Costs
item.description: arXiv:2505.21331v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In queueing systems, the holding costs of jobs may evolve in uncertain ways. For example, in content moderation for social media platforms, the cost of delaying the review of a content piece is proportional to its view trajectory, which fluctuates and is a priori unknown. To capture such uncertain and evolving holding cost patterns, we consider a queueing model where job states evolve based on a Markov chain with state-dependent instantaneous holding costs. We demonstrate that in the presence of such uncertain and evolving holding costs, the two canonical algorithmic principles, instantaneous-cost ($c\mu$-rule) and expected-remaining-cost ($c\mu/\theta$-rule), are suboptimal. By viewing each job as a Markovian ski-rental problem, we develop a new index-based algorithm, Opportunity-adjusted Remaining Cost (OaRC), that adjusts to the opportunity of serving jobs in the future when uncertainty partly resolves. We show that the suboptimality gap of OaRC scales as $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{N})$, where $N$ is the system size. This bound shows that OaRC achieves asymptotic optimality for overloaded systems when the system size $N$ scales to infinity. Moreover, the bound is independent of the state-space size, which is a desirable property when job states contain contextual information. We corroborate our results with an extensive simulation study based on two holding cost patterns (online ads and user-generated content) that arise in content moderation for social media platforms. Our simulations based on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that OaRC consistently outperforms existing practice, which is based on the two canonical algorithmic principles.
item.dc:creator: Caner Gocmen, Thodoris Lykouris, Deeksha Sinha, Wentao Weng

item.title: Efficient space reduction techniques by optimized majority rules for the Kemeny aggregation problem
item.description: arXiv:2506.15097v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Kemeny aggregation problem consists of computing the consensus rankings of an election with respect to the Kemeny-Young voting method. These consensus rankings satisfy various fundamental properties and are the geometric medians of the votes in the election under the Kendall tau distance, which counts the number of pairwise disagreements. The NP-hard Kemeny aggregation problem admits important applications in various domains such as operations research, computational social choice, machine learning, and biology but faces a severe bottleneck in practice. In 2020, Milosz and the second author presented an approach to reduce the search space of the problem by solving the relative order of pairs of elements in those consensus rankings. In this article, we prove an optimized and fully parallelizable extension of this approach. We achieve significantly more space reduction while the parallel design reduces the time complexity from ${O}(n^3)$ to essentially ${O}(n^2)$ with significant computational speedups in practice. We then show how the constraints built by our approach can be rigorously combined with other methods such as Integer Programming and Finest Condorcet Partitioning to achieve a highly efficient, robust, and scalable solution approach to the Kemeny aggregation problem. Our methods are applicable to the more general constrained Kemeny aggregation ranking problem with immutable input pairwise constraints. Experiments with benchmark against the commercial solver Gurobi are performed on real and synthetic data.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Kien Phung, Sylvie Hamel

item.title: Attractors Is All You Need: Parity Games In Polynomial Time
item.description: arXiv:2511.03752v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides a polynomial-time algorithm for solving parity games that runs in $\mathcal{O}(n^{2}\cdot(n + m))$ time-ending a search that has taken decades. Unlike previous attractor-based algorithms, the presented algorithm only removes regions with a determined winner. The paper introduces a new type of attractor that can guarantee finding the minimal dominion of a parity game. The attractor runs in polynomial time and can peel the graph empty.
item.dc:creator: Rick van der Heijden

item.title: Graph-based Nearest Neighbors with Dynamic Updates via Random Walks
item.description: arXiv:2512.18060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANN) is a common way to retrieve relevant search results, especially now in the context of large language models and retrieval augmented generation. One of the most widely used algorithms for ANN is based on constructing a multi-layer graph over the dataset, called the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW). While this algorithm supports insertion of new data, it does not support deletion of existing data. Moreover, deletion algorithms described by prior work come at the cost of increased query latency, decreased recall, or prolonged deletion time. In this paper, we propose a new theoretical framework for graph-based ANN based on random walks. We then utilize this framework to analyze a randomized deletion approach that approximately preserves hitting time statistics compared to the graph before deleting the point. However, this guarantee needs at least as many edge samples as there are edges in the clique over the neighbors of the deleted point. We then turn this theoretical framework into a deterministic deletion algorithm, and show that it provides a better tradeoff between query latency, recall, deletion time, and memory usage through an extensive collection of experiments.
item.dc:creator: Nina Mishra, Yonatan Naamad, Tal Wagner, Lichen Zhang

item.title: Gabow's $O(\sqrt{n}m)$ Maximum Cardinality Matching Algorithm, Revisited
item.description: arXiv:2603.22909v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit Gabow's $O(\sqrt{n} m)$ maximum cardinality matching algorithm (The Weighted Matching Approach to Maximum Cardinality Matching, Fundamenta Informaticae, 2017). It adapts the weighted matching algorithm of Gabow and Tarjan~\cite{GT91} to maximum cardinality matching. Gabow's algorithm works iteratively. In each iteration, it constructs a maximal number of edge-disjoint shortest augmenting paths with respect to the current matching and augments them. It is well-known that $O(\sqrt{n})$ iterations suffice. Each iteration consists of three parts. In the first part, the length of the shortest augmenting path is computed. In the second part, an auxiliary graph $H$ is constructed with the property that shortest augmenting paths in $G$ correspond to augmenting paths in $H$. In the third part, a maximal set of edge-disjoint augmenting paths in $H$ is determined, and the paths are lifted to and augmented to $G$. We give a new algorithm for the first part. Gabow's algorithm for the first part is derived from Edmonds' primal-dual algorithm for weighted matching. We believe that our approach is more direct and will be easier to teach. We have implemented the algorithm; the implementation is available at the companion webpage (https://people.mpi-inf.mpg.de/~mehlhorn/CompanionPageGenMatchingImplementation.html).
item.dc:creator: Kurt Mehlhorn, Romina Nobahari

item.title: Well-Conditioned Oblivious Perturbations in Linear Space
item.description: arXiv:2604.23193v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Perturbing a deterministic $n$-dimensional matrix with small Gaussian noise is a cornerstone of smoothed analysis of algorithms [Spielman and Teng, JACM 2004], as it reduces the condition number of the input to $O(n)$, and with it the complexity of many matrix algorithms. However, when deployed algorithmically, these perturbations are expensive due to the cost of generating and storing $n^2$ Gaussian random variables. We propose a perturbation that requires generating and storing $O(n)$ random numbers in $O(\log n)$ bits of precision, and reduces the condition number of any deterministic matrix to $O(n)$, matching Gaussian perturbations. Our result takes a step towards derandomizing matrix perturbations in numerical linear algebra, and in particular, implies that we can solve an $n\times n$ linear system to within $\varepsilon$ backward error in $O(n^2\log(n)/\varepsilon)$ time using only $O(n\log n)$ random bits. In our construction, we introduce the concept of a pattern matrix, which is a dense deterministic matrix that maps all sparse vectors into dense vectors in a way that goes beyond the classical uncertainty principle of the Fourier transform. We combine this with a sparse perturbation whose entries are dependent and located in a non-uniform fashion. In order to analyze this construction, we develop new techniques for lower bounding the smallest singular value of a random matrix with dependent entries.
item.dc:creator: Shabarish Chenakkod, Micha{\l} Derezi\'nski, Xiaoyu Dong, Mark Rudelson

item.title: Tolerant Testing for Bipartiteness and Unique Games
item.description: arXiv:2605.17760v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a tolerant bipartiteness tester in the adjacency-list model on arbitrary simple undirected graphs. Let \(n\) be the number of vertices and \(m>0\) the known number of edges. For \(0<\varepsilon<\rho<1/10\), write \(\lambda_\rho:=\rho/(1+\log(1/\rho))\). If \(\varepsilon\log n\le c\lambda_\rho^2\) for a sufficiently small absolute constant \(c>0\), the tester distinguishes graphs that can be made bipartite by deleting at most an \(\varepsilon\) fraction of their edges from graphs requiring deletion of at least a \(\rho\) fraction, using \[ \widetilde O\!\left( \frac{\sqrt{n/\rho}}{\lambda_\rho^{3/2}} +\frac1{\lambda_\rho^2} +\frac{n}{\sqrt m\,\lambda_\rho}\right) \] queries, where the suppressed factors are polylogarithmic in \(n,1/\rho\). For fixed \(\rho\), the query bound is \(\widetilde O(\sqrt n+n/\sqrt m)\). We prove an \(\Omega(\sqrt n+n/\sqrt m)\) query lower bound. The tester extends to Unique Games over any alphabet size \(Q\ge2\), under the same tolerance condition with \(c\) independent of \(Q\), with a polylogarithmic overhead in \(Q\) in the query complexity. Each constrained neighbor query returns the entire edge permutation.
item.dc:creator: Yuichi Yoshida

item.title: Learning-Augmented Online Minimization with Dual Predictions
item.description: arXiv:2606.05380v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present learning-augmented algorithms for two general classes of online minimization problems: metrical task systems and laminar set cover. Both algorithms achieve improved theoretical guarantees using machine-learned predictions of an optimal solution to the dual linear program. Unlike optimal primal solutions, which can change drastically under tiny instance perturbations, these dual solutions are much more stable, which ensures the existence of good (and learnable) predictions for families of similar instances. While previous work has used dual predictions in offline settings and for online maximization problems, our algorithms are, to the best of our knowledge, the first demonstration that such dual predictions can be effective for online minimization. Our theoretical results are complemented by experiments on the $k$-server problem and the parking permit problem.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026) 21020-21045
item.dc:creator: Christian Coester, Alexa Tudose, Alexander Turoczy

item.title: Breadth-First Search in Succinct Planar Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.06221v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An encoding for a graph class $\mathcal{G}$ is called succinct if it uses $Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n)+o(Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n))$ bits, where $Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n)$ is the information-theoretic minimum number of bits needed to distinguish between $n$-vertex graphs of $\mathcal{G}$; it is called compact if it uses $O(Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n))$ bits. For planar graphs, $Z_{\mathcal{G}}(n)=\Theta(n)$. We present a succinct encoding of planar graphs that supports executing a breadth-first search directly on the encoding. The succinct encoding can be constructed in expected $O(n)$ time using $O(n)$ bits during construction; a compact variant can be constructed in deterministic $O(n)$ time using $O(n)$ bits. Once the encoding is constructed, a BFS from any start vertex can be computed in $O(n)$ time using $o(n)$ additional bits, including the space needed to represent the BFS tree. The resulting BFS tree $T$ remains available for standard tree operations, such as traversal, parent and child queries, layer queries, and lowest common ancestor queries, in constant time per query and amortized constant time per output element. The encoding also supports standard graph queries. Finally, all BFS and tree-query results generalize to separable graph classes, with graph-class-specific construction time and space for the encoding.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Meintrup

item.title: Improved Approximation of Min-Distances in Near-Linear Time
item.description: arXiv:2607.09588v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of approximating the diameter of directed graphs under the min-distance measure, defined as $d_{\min}(u,v) = \min(d(u,v), d(v,u))$. Unlike standard shortest-path distance, min-distance is not a metric, which renders many classical techniques inapplicable. Prior work has therefore focused on approximating this parameter, culminating in an approximation-runtime tradeoff by Dalirrooyfard et al. [ICALP'19] giving a $4k-1$ approximation in $\tilde{O}(mn^{1/(k+1)})$ time for any positive integer $k$ and, more recently, the first near-linear time constant approximation by Chechik and Zhang [FOCS'22], where they obtained a 4-approximation to the min-diameter. In this work we present a randomized near-linear time algorithm that achieves a $3$-approximation to the min-diameter, outperforming all known approximation-runtime tradeoffs. Our approach introduces a novel type-classification framework that may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Yael Kirkpatrick

item.title: Tight Bounds for $(1+\epsilon)$-Approximation for Minimum Spanning Trees in Doubling Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2607.13284v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The minimum spanning tree (MST) problem is one of the most basic optimization problems on metric spaces and graphs. We study the problem of computing a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation to the MST of an $n$-point metric space of doubling dimension $\mathrm{ddim}$. In doubling metrics, previous deterministic algorithms incur a running time with dependence $\epsilon^{-O(\mathrm{ddim})}$. We give a deterministic algorithm that computes a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate MST in time $$ O_{\mathrm{ddim}}\left(n\log n+ \min\left\{n^2,\frac{n}{\epsilon}\log(1/\epsilon)\right\}\right) $$ in the standard real RAM model with a unit-cost exact-distance oracle. For bounded doubling dimension, this improves the previous dependence on $\epsilon$ to essentially linear in $\epsilon^{-1}$. We complement this algorithm with a lower bound of $$ \Omega \!\left(n\log n+ \min\left\{n^2,\frac{n}{\epsilon}\log(1/\epsilon)\right\}\right) $$ on running time in the same model, already for metrics of doubling dimension at most seven, showing that our running time is essentially tight. For points in $\mathbb R^d$ with $d = O(1)$, exploiting Euclidean geometry allows us to further improve the dependence on $\epsilon$. We obtain a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate MST in expected time $$ O_d\left( n \log n + \min\left\{n^2, \frac{n}{\epsilon^{1 - \beta_d}} \log^{1-\beta_d}(1/\epsilon) \right\} \right) $$ for some $\beta_d=\Theta(1/d)$, improving the accuracy-dependent term $n\epsilon^{-2}\log^2(1/\epsilon)$ of Arya and Mount [SODA'16].
item.dc:creator: Jan H\"ockendorff, Felix Hommelsheim, Christian Sohler, Di Yue

item.title: Strong Testability of Full Quartet Consistency with Polynomial Query Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2608.00987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study dense property testing of full quartet systems on~$n$ taxa, where one resolved topology is specified for every four-set. We give an explicit polynomial-time adaptive one-sided tester using $O(\varepsilon^{-1}\log(2/\varepsilon)\log(1/\delta))$ quartet queries to distinguish tree-like inputs from inputs that are $\varepsilon$-far from every tree-induced system, with soundness error at most $\delta$, for $0<\delta\leq1/3$. The bound is independent of $n$. The tester reconstructs trees on a small random sample and its verification taxa, then checks their individual attachment edges. Soundness follows by comparing with a global tree fixed by the initial sample and bounding attachment collisions through a conditional symmetry argument. Querying the complete sampled subsystem in advance also gives an explicit non-adaptive $O(\varepsilon^{-4}\log(1/\delta))$ bound. A distance-preserving encoding into directed colored structures provides an additional qualitative proof through hereditary testing. For ordinary testing, we prove an $\Omega(\varepsilon^{-1}\log(1/\delta))$ query lower bound for $0<\varepsilon,\delta\leq1/4$ and sufficiently large $n$. We also analyze the stronger requirement of reconstructing the exact tree on tree-like inputs, obtaining tight bounds up to constants of $\Theta(n\log n+\varepsilon^{-1}\log(1/\delta))$ adaptively and $\Theta(n^3+\varepsilon^{-1}\log(1/\delta))$ non-adaptively.
item.dc:creator: Chuang-Chieh Lin

item.title: The Complexity of Computing Class Probabilities in BID Probabilistic Databases
item.description: arXiv:2609.21245v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of computing class probabilities in block-independent disjoint (BID) probabilistic databases. Given the probability with which each block in the database realizes each feasible tuple type, the goal is to compute the probability of a class of worlds specified by a given tuple multiplicity vector, thus grouping together worlds with the same bag (multiset) of realized tuple types. For this problem, we prove $\#\mathsf{P}$-hardness even for very restricted and structured inputs. On the other hand, we show that it admits an FPRAS, as well as $\mathsf{XP}$-time algorithms parameterized by the number of tuple types and the treewidth of an incidence graph modeling the connections between blocks and tuples. Finally, we show that augmenting the problem with certain compatibility constraints between block realizations renders it $\#\mathsf{XLP}$- and $\#\mathsf{XALP}$-hard parameterized by pathwidth and treewidth respectively, ruling out $\mathsf{FPT}$ algorithms under standard assumptions. We leave as an open question whether this also holds in the absence of compatibility constraints.
item.dc:creator: Sotiris Kanellopoulos, Ioannis Koutras, Aris Pagourtzis

item.title: A (2 sqrt(3) - 3)-Approximation for Online and Offline Non-Monotone DR-Submodular Maximization
item.description: arXiv:2610.21072v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain the approximation coefficient $\alpha_0=2\sqrt3-3$ for maximizing nonnegative,non-monotone DR-submodular functions over compact convex down-closed subsets of the unit cube, with queries allowed throughout the cube. This improves the previous best coefficient, $4/9$. A coordinatewise map, exponential on small coordinates and linear-fractional on large ones, turns a feasible point, the learner's state, into a feasible action whose value is at least $\alpha_0$ times that of any feasible point, up to a linear term. No map of the state that is feasible for every down-closed set admits a larger coefficient in such a comparison. The proof combines lemmas proved by hand with finitely many sign conditions on explicit piecewise polynomials, verified in exact arithmetic. The linear term has an unbiased estimator from one noisy-gradient query, which reduces online maximization to online linear optimization. With gradient responses of bounded conditional second moment, projected ascent has expected approximate regret $O(\sqrt T)$, and online Frank--Wolfe with one linear-maximization call per round has $O(T^{3/4})$ when the responses are almost surely bounded. One noisy value per round, with bounded gradients and second-moment or almost-sure bounds on the value responses, gives $O(T^{3/4})$ and $O(T^{7/8})$, respectively. Online-to-batch conversion turns these bounds into offline guarantees. With exact values and gradients, contracting the objective toward a feasible interior point yields an expected $(\alpha_0-\varepsilon)$-approximation for every nonnegative $C^1$ DR-submodular objective, with oracle counts polynomial in $n$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and no gradient or smoothness parameter.
